nodes.label: Identity, Not Auth (deliberate simplification)
nodes.rationale: Skipped full auth (bcrypt/JWT/sessions) because event is small (about 50 known participants, one room, a few hours). Pre-registered name dropdown + optional 4-digit PIN stored in localStorage. Admin uses shared env-var PIN. PostgreSQL still required for participant list, submissions, challenges, and competition state.

nodes.label: Comparison Tools (Split Slider, Opacity Slider, Difference Mode)
nodes.rationale: Client-side visual aids to help participants judge accuracy before submitting. Pixelmatch is reused client-side for Difference Mode so the diff library is consistent with server-side scoring.

nodes.label: Tech Stack Table (Project Plan section 4)
nodes.rationale: React+Vite, Monaco, React Query, React Router, Tailwind, Node+Express, Prisma, PostgreSQL, Playwright, Pixelmatch, Docker, self-hosted on local LAN. Monaco chosen back over CodeMirror/Ace due to small scale (10-15 participants).

nodes.label: Submission -> Scoring Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Sanitize input -> write temp HTML -> headless Chromium via Playwright in isolated service -> screenshot at fixed viewport -> Pixelmatch diff against target -> store score + screenshot -> update leaderboard. Isolation matters most because this executes untrusted code.

nodes.label: Database Schema (User, Challenge, Submission, CompetitionState)
nodes.rationale: User has unique name and optional pin_code (not hashed, low-stakes). Submission flags is_best per user-challenge. Ranking: highest similarity, then shortest code length, then earliest submission time.

nodes.label: Backend Module Structure (Project Plan section 6)
nodes.rationale: backend/src/{identity,users,challenges,submissions,scoring,rendering,leaderboard,admin,db,middleware,routes}. Scoring, rendering, challenges, and submissions kept separate so the algorithm and renderer can be swapped independently.

nodes.label: Frontend Structure (Project Plan section 7)
nodes.rationale: frontend/src/{pages,components/{Editor,Preview,CompareTools,LeaderboardTable,shared},hooks,services}. Live preview uses sandboxed iframe with srcDoc, debounced 300-500ms, sandbox='allow-same-origin' only (no allow-scripts).

nodes.label: Capacity Reality Check (i9-14900K, 64GB RAM)
nodes.rationale: Per render: 0.5-1s and 150-300MB RAM. With 24 threads, machine handles 150-200 simultaneous renders. At 10-15 participants this is 1-2% of capacity. Validates skipping Redis/BullMQ. Real event-day risk shifts to network reliability, AP/client isolation, firewall, and machine access, not compute.

nodes.label: No-Job-Queue Decision
nodes.rationale: Synchronous rendering per request, no Redis/BullMQ. Justified by hardware capacity math, not by time pressure. Revisit only if scale grows to 200+ concurrent participants or hardware is downgraded.

nodes.label: Security Considerations (Project Plan section 11)
nodes.rationale: Isolated disposable Playwright instance, JS disabled, external network blocked, hard timeout/memory/CPU limits, submission size caps, never reuse browser state, rate-limit submit endpoint per user.

nodes.label: 25-Day Timeline
nodes.rationale: Days 1-3 setup/identity/DB/Docker; 4-7 challenge CRUD/admin; 8-12 Monaco+preview+comparison; 13-16 rendering/scoring (hardest, do early); 17-19 leaderboard; 20-22 testing+load test; 23-25 buffer.
